title: fix(causal-graphs): resolve PR #667 adversarial review findings on CausalEdge IDs, skill prefixes, and organism-scope writer resolution
body:
## Summary

Independent adversarial review of PR #667 at commit `989c4e71ca9ce111711738ec5814583fdb958b23` identified three findings to resolve before merging the Stage 2 `causal_graphs` prerequisite stack (#658):

1. **[Blocking] `CausalEdge.id` format alignment and `CausalEdge:` prefix handling**:
   - `.claude/skills/curate-causal-graphs/SKILL.md` (lines 24, 46, 81) and `scripts/apply_causal_graphs.py` docstring (line 18) show `CultureMech:001645_causal_1` / `CultureMech:001234_causal_1`, whereas `src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml` and `src/culturemech/validation/causal_graphs.py` enforce `^(edge_[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+|CausalEdge:[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)$`.
   - `scripts/validate_id_label_correspondence.py` (`_walk_yaml`) treats any `id` containing `:` as a CURIE and emits `UNKNOWN_PREFIX` for `CausalEdge:` unless `CausalEdge` is listed in `conf/id_label_targets.yaml` (`ignored_prefixes`), `conf/oak_config.yaml` (`ontology_adapters`), and `src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml` (`prefixes`).
2. **[Non-blocking] Align `CausalTerm` prefix list in `.claude/skills/curate-causal-graphs/SKILL.md`**:
   - Line 25 of `.claude/skills/curate-causal-graphs/SKILL.md` should list the exact 15 `CausalTerm` prefixes enforced by `src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml` and `CAUSAL_TERM_ID_RE` (`CHEBI`, `NCBITaxon`, `GO`, `UniProtKB`, `EC`, `KEGG`, `METPO`, `ENVO`, `PATO`, `NCIT`, `FOODON`, `UBERON`, `MICRO`, `CultureMech`, `MediaIngredientMech`) and omit `RO` (which is used for predicate meanings rather than `subject_term`/`object_term` endpoints).
3. **[Non-blocking] `scripts/apply_causal_graphs.py` organism-scoped proposal resolution and deduplication**:
   - When `target_scope == "organism"` and `organism_taxon_id` is omitted, derive `org_taxon` from `causal_edge.organism_term.id` (raising `ValueError` if neither is provided) rather than matching `target_organisms[0]` unconditionally, and include `enclosing_org` in `_edge_signature` / `_dedup_append`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Update `.claude/skills/curate-causal-graphs/SKILL.md` and `scripts/apply_causal_graphs.py` examples to use `edge_<slug>` IDs and exact `CausalTerm` prefix documentation.
- [ ] Add `CausalEdge` prefix to `src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml` (and regenerate schema artifacts), `conf/id_label_targets.yaml` (`ignored_prefixes`), and `conf/oak_config.yaml` (`ontology_adapters`), and add an ID-label correspondence test in `tests/test_causal_graphs.py`.
- [ ] Resolve `organism_taxon_id` fallback and `enclosing_org` deduplication in `scripts/apply_causal_graphs.py` with unit test coverage.

title: infra(stage-3): define UniProtKB prefix, typed ProteinExample schema, OAK validation, writer, and skill prerequisites
body:
## Summary

Cycle 2 Stage 3 (`protein_examples`) in `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml` (and pinned in `/Users/marcin/Documents/VIMSS/ontology/KG-Hub/KG-Microbe/culturebotai-claw/workspace/session-orchestration/20261019/culturemech/effective-workflow.json`) is currently marked `applicability: blocked` with `skill_paths: []` and reason:

> CultureMech has no UniProt prefix, protein-example schema slot, or repository-local protein-example curation skill.

A repository-wide prerequisite audit (`audit-schema-gaps` + `culturemech-evolve-workflow`, including hidden and git-ignored paths) at commit `231e0ba71b41d45362168d539efebe7991823464` verified that free-text gene/enzyme strings currently in the schema do not constitute typed UniProt protein-example support.

## Current Native Capabilities & Limitations

- **Native schema (`src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml`, lines 10–58, 1234–1296, 1565–1602, 2000–2072)**:
  - Declares 31 prefixes (`linkml`, `culturemech`, `biolink`, `rdfs`, `CHEBI`, `NCBITaxon`, `DSMZ`, `TOGO`, `ATCC`, `NCIT`, `UTEX`, `CCAP`, `SAG`, `OBI`, `ENVO`, `UO`, `UBERON`, `FOODON`, `mediadive.compound`, `PMID`, `DOI`, `KEGG`, `EC`, `geo`, `sra`, `GTDB`, `RefSeq`, `GenBank`, `BioSample`, `sigma`, `thermofisher`). **No `UniProt` or `UniProtKB` prefix or `UniProtTerm` class exists.**
  - `CofactorDescriptor` (lines 1234–1296) defines `enzyme_examples` (`range: string`, `multivalued: true`), `biosynthesis_genes` (`range: string`, `multivalued: true`), and `ec_associations` (`range: string`, `multivalued: true` with EC pattern).
  - `CofactorRequirement` (lines 2000–2028) defines `genes` (`range: string`, `multivalued: true`).
  - `TransporterAnnotation` (lines 2029–2072) defines `name` (`range: string`), `genes` (`range: string`, `multivalued: true`), `ec_number` (`range: string`), and `evidence` (`EvidenceItem`).
  - `StrainModification` (lines 1565–1602) defines `target` (`range: string`, description `"Gene, operon, or pathway modified"`).
- **Corpus & reference data audit (`15,915` normalized records + `data/reference/cofactors.yaml`)**:
  - Across all `15,915` normalized YAML records in `data/normalized_yaml/`, `cofactors_provided`, `cofactor_requirements`, `transporters`, `enzyme_examples`, `biosynthesis_genes`, and `ec_associations` have **`0` populated instances**; `strain_modifications` is populated in `2` records (`archaea/pyrococcus_medium.yaml` with `target: cellulose utilization`, `bacterial/magnetospirillum_gryphiswaldense_medium.yaml` with `target: mamAB operon`) using free-text strings.
  - `data/reference/cofactors.yaml` (56 entries across 8 categories generated by `src/culturemech/import/import_cofactors.py`) uses `enzyme_examples` only for generic free-text enzyme family labels (e.g., `"pyruvate dehydrogenase"`, `"methanol dehydrogenase (XoxF-MDH)"`), with `0` UniProt accessions, `0` organism (`NCBITaxon`) bindings, `0` claim-level `EvidenceItem` records, and unvalidated ChEBI mappings (including duplicate `CHEBI:60052` across `heme_c` (`heme C`) and `heme_d1` (`heme d1`)).
  - `docs/ENRICHMENT_GUIDE.md` references `normalized_yaml/bacterial/Nitrate_Mineral_Salts_Medium_(NMS)_ENRICHED_EXAMPLE.yaml`, which does not exist in the repository.
- **Validation & Exporter Gaps**:
  - `conf/oak_config.yaml` and `conf/id_label_targets.yaml` have no `UniProtKB` adapter or prefix rule; adding `UniProtKB:` IDs into `(id, label)` validated targets without adapter configuration would fail `scripts/validate_id_label.py` with `UNKNOWN_PREFIX`.
  - `src/culturemech/export/kgx_export.py` (lines 468–833) does not emit protein nodes (`biolink:Protein`) or medium/cofactor/transporter-to-protein edges.

## Missing Prerequisites to Unblock Stage 3 (`protein_examples`)

1. **LinkML Schema Support (`src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml`)**:
   - Add prefix `UniProtKB: https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/` to `prefixes:`.
   - Define `UniProtTerm` (`id` required with pattern `^UniProtKB:([OPQ][0-9][A-Z0-9]{3}[0-9]|[A-NR-Z][0-9]([A-Z][A-Z0-9]{2}[0-9]){1,2})(-\d+)?$`, `label` required for canonical protein name) and `ProteinExample` (or typed `protein_examples` slot on `CofactorDescriptor`, `TransporterAnnotation`, and/or `OrganismDescriptor`) that binds:
     - `uniprot_term` (`UniProtTerm`),
     - explicit `organism_term` (`NCBITaxonTerm` so every UniProt accession is tied to the exact strain/taxon in the medium),
     - optional `gene_symbol`, `ec_number`, and `role_in_medium` (e.g., cofactor-dependent enzyme, uptake transporter),
     - mandatory claim-scoped `evidence` (`EvidenceItem` with `reference` `PMID:`/`DOI:`/`gomodel:`, `supports`, and verbatim `snippet`).
2. **Validation & ID-Label Correspondence (`conf/id_label_targets.yaml`, `conf/oak_config.yaml`, `scripts/validate_strict.py`)**:
   - Configure `UniProtTerm` validation rules (syntax + accession/taxon/label verification or explicit `id_label_targets.yaml` handling) and `scripts/validate_strict.py` checks ensuring every `ProteinExample` carries a verified `UniProtKB:` ID, matching `NCBITaxon:` organism, and non-empty `EvidenceItem`.
   - Remediate or isolate `data/reference/cofactors.yaml` ChEBI label drift (`CHEBI:60052` collision) before importing cofactor protein examples into `data/normalized_yaml/`.
3. **Maintained Writer & KGX Exporter (`scripts/`, `src/culturemech/export/kgx_export.py`)**:
   - Implement a schema-validating writer that updates `data/normalized_yaml/` and appends `curation_history`, plus `kgx_export.py` emission of `biolink:Protein` nodes and typed edges without mutating generated outputs (`data/merge_yaml/merged/`, `app/`, `pages/`, `output/`) directly.
4. **Repository-Local Skill & Profile Unblocking (`.claude/skills/`, `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml`)**:
   - Create a `.claude/skills/` skill for curating evidence-backed UniProt protein examples on media cofactors/transporters, add `tests/` coverage, and update `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml` Stage 3 `skill_paths` and `applicability` for the next cycle reload.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `UniProtKB` prefix, `UniProtTerm`, and `ProteinExample` classes validate cleanly under `scripts/audit_schema.py` and `scripts/validate_strict.py`.
- Maintained writer, KGX exporter, validator config, unit tests, and `.claude/skills/` skill are in place before Stage 3 (`protein_examples`) is marked `applicable` in `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml`.

title: infra(stage-2): define native causal_graphs schema, writer, validator, KGX export, and skill prerequisites
body:
## Summary

Cycle 2 Stage 2 (`causal_graphs`) in `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml` (and pinned in `/Users/marcin/Documents/VIMSS/ontology/KG-Hub/KG-Microbe/culturebotai-claw/workspace/session-orchestration/20261019/culturemech/effective-workflow.json`) is currently marked `applicability: blocked` with `skill_paths: []` and reason:

> CultureMech models growth-media compositions and preparation protocols rather than causal mechanism graphs; no native causal-graph schema slot or curation skill is defined.

A repository-wide prerequisite audit (`audit-schema-gaps` + `culturemech-evolve-workflow`, including hidden and git-ignored paths) at commit `231e0ba71b41d45362168d539efebe7991823464` verified what CultureMech can currently represent versus what is required for evidence-backed causal mechanism graphs.

## Current Native Capabilities (Composition & Role Facets Only)

- **Native schema (`src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml`, `src/culturemech/schema/mim_roles.yaml`)**:
  - `IngredientDescriptor` (lines 865–1193) supports composition amounts (`concentration`), ChEBI/MediaIngredientMech term references (`chebi_term`, `mediaingredientmech_term`), three role facet enums (`nutritional_roles` (`NutritionalRoleEnum`), `physicochemical_roles` (`PhysicochemicalRoleEnum`), `cellular_metabolic_roles` (`CellularMetabolicRoleEnum`)), and `cofactors_provided` (`CofactorDescriptor`).
  - `OrganismDescriptor` (lines 1344–1564) supports `growth_metrics` (`GrowthMetrics`, with `nutrient_overrides` (`NutrientOverride`: `role`, `source`, `is_sole_source`, `notes`)), `perturbations` (`Perturbation` with `modification_type`, `description`, `growth_outcome`, `effect_description`, `evidence`), and `strain_modifications` (`StrainModification` with `modification_type`, `target`, `description`, `ontology_id`, `evidence`).
  - Corpus population across all `15,915` normalized YAML records in `data/normalized_yaml/`: `nutritional_roles` (`217`), `physicochemical_roles` (`249`), `cellular_metabolic_roles` (`5`), `perturbations` (`3`), `strain_modifications` (`2`), `nutrient_overrides` (`2`), `cofactors_provided` (`0`).
- **Maintained writers & exporters**:
  - `scripts/render_media_role_graph.py` (`.claude/skills/render-media-role-graph/SKILL.md`) renders bipartite Mermaid composition/role diagrams (`MediaRecipe` -> `IngredientDescriptor` -> role facet enum values + `OrganismDescriptor` `community_role` / `nutrient_overrides`), not directed causal mechanism chains.
  - `src/culturemech/export/kgx_export.py` (lines 468–833) defines 12 `*_to_edge` functions emitting 7 predicates (`METPO:2000517` organism-to-medium, `biolink:has_part` medium-to-solution/ingredient/role, `biolink:has_attribute` medium-to-type/state/pH, `biolink:related_to` cofactor hierarchies, `biolink:same_as`, `biolink:subclass_of`, and `biolink:has_dataset`), with `0` causal predicate edges (`biolink:causes`, `biolink:affects`, `biolink:regulates`, etc.).
  - `scripts/repair_top_causal_graph_score15.py` only curates media composition, stock solutions, role enums, pH, preparation steps, and sterilization; its filename is a historical misnomer that appears in `curation_history.curator` of 4 bacterial records (`my20_agar.yaml`, `my75s.yaml`, `mycoplasma_medium_atcc_243_with_sucrose.yaml`, `na_0_5_yeast_extract.yaml`).
  - `src/culturemech/schema/mech_shared.yaml` mentions `causal_graphs#edge_x` only in the shared `Discussion.attaches_to` docstring inherited across Mech repositories; `MediaRecipe` has no `causal_graphs` or `mechanism_graph` slot.

## Missing Prerequisites to Unblock Stage 2 (`causal_graphs`) (or Reclassify Scope)

1. **Domain & Architecture Decision (`culturemech-infra-0002` Step 1)**:
   - Confirm with parent KG-Microbe / Mech architecture whether growth-media records in CultureMech should natively represent directed causal mechanism edges (e.g., ingredient/perturbation -> transporter/cofactor/metabolic process -> organism growth phenotype) **or** whether `causal_graphs` should be formally classified in `workflow/parent/mech-cycle.yaml` / `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml` as `not_applicable` for composition-centric repositories.
2. **LinkML Schema Extension (`src/culturemech/schema/culturemech.yaml`)** *(if native Stage 2 is adopted)*:
   - Define a typed `CausalEdge` / `MechanismEdge` class with explicit `id`, typed `subject` (ingredient, cofactor, perturbation, or solution term), constrained causal `predicate` (`biolink:` / `RO:` causal relation enum), typed `object` (metabolic process `GO:`, cofactor `CHEBI:`, transporter/protein target, or growth phenotype), optional `organism_context` (`NCBITaxon:`), experimental condition scope, and mandatory claim-scoped `evidence` (`EvidenceItem` with `reference` `PMID:`/`DOI:`/`gomodel:`, `supports`, and verbatim `snippet`).
   - Attach multivalued slot `causal_graphs` (or `causal_edges`) to `MediaRecipe` without altering existing composition/role slots.
3. **Validation & OAK Target Configuration (`conf/id_label_targets.yaml`, `scripts/validate_strict.py`, `scripts/validate_id_label.py`)**:
   - Register any new ontology-grounded subject/object `(id, label)` pairs in `conf/id_label_targets.yaml` and enforce `EvidenceItem` completeness (`reference` + `snippet` + `supports`) in `scripts/validate_strict.py`.
4. **Maintained Writer & KGX Exporter (`scripts/`, `src/culturemech/export/kgx_export.py`)**:
   - Provide a schema-validating writer that updates `data/normalized_yaml/` and appends `curation_history` (`audit_writers.py` compliant), preserves generated-output ownership (`data/merge_yaml/merged/`, `app/`, `pages/`, `output/`), and exports verified causal edges in `src/culturemech/export/kgx_export.py` with unit tests.
5. **Repository-Local Skill & Profile Unblocking (`.claude/skills/`, `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml`)**:
   - Add a repository-local `.claude/skills/` skill for evidence-backed causal mechanism curation with explicit negative controls against fabricating edges from generic ingredient roles, add `tests/` coverage, and update `workflow/mech-workflow.yaml` Stage 2 `skill_paths` and `applicability` for the next cycle reload.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either (A) native `CausalEdge` schema class, validator targets, maintained writer, KGX exporter, `.claude/skills/` curation skill, and unit tests are implemented and pass `scripts/validate_strict.py`, `scripts/audit_schema.py`, `scripts/audit_writers.py`, and `pytest`, **or** (B) parent coordinator policy explicitly reclassifies Stage 2 for CultureMech composition records without fabricating scientific fields.
- Authoritative inputs remain strictly in `data/normalized_yaml/`; no unverified causal edges are invented from role enums.

title: Culture-type inference must respect variant-only targets and explicit uncertainty
body: PR #620 adds named targets and exposes 34 unset culture types. The existing inference treats any named target as evidence for a parent isolate medium, including variant-scoped growth. Exclude variant-only targets from parent classification, retain community/uncertain cases for curation, and populate culture type only where the source supports it. Add scope regressions and update paper-citation skill guidance. Do not widen variant growth to the canonical parent merely to satisfy CI.

Preserve original concentration receipts and their source audits; register narrowly audited, hash-linked citation successors without exempting recipe amounts or prior history. Select the website source-correction event by identity, not list position. Add mutation regressions against unreviewed quantity/history changes. title: Reconcile AF6 base formulation before assigning study variants or growth
body: PR #620 adds AF6-family bibliography with unresolved formulation scope, not new growth or concentration assertions. title: 6 MediaDive solution records and 57 prose fields still contain U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN (#409 only cleaned TOGO)
body:
Found while re-checking #387 before closing it. #409 (`2e4566eaad`) strips invisible characters from TOGO component names, using `clean_component_name` in `src/culturemech/import/togo_importer.py`. No other importer does this, and U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN is still in the corpus.

A YAML walk of `data/normalized_yaml` on `main` at `41d4d39` finds 69 string values containing U+00AD. It finds none of the other characters that `_INVISIBLE` strips (U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+2060 and U+FEFF).

## Record names: 6 records, 12 fields

Each record below has U+00AD in both `preferred_term` and `term.label`:

| record (`data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/`) | id | source id |
|---|---|---|
| `mediadive_6188_3N_BBM_V_Bold_Basal_Medium_with_3_fold_Nitrogen_and_Vitamins_modified.yaml` | CultureMech:014887 | mediadive.solution:6188 |
| `mediadive_6197_MY75S_Malt_Yeast_Extract_75_Seawater_Agar.yaml` | CultureMech:014894 | mediadive.solution:6197 |
| `mediadive_6207_NCL_New_Cereal_Leaf-_Prescott_Liquid.yaml` | CultureMech:014905 | mediadive.solution:6207 |
| `mediadive_6209_0_01_NPA_New_Cereal_Leaf-_Prescott_Agar.yaml` | CultureMech:014906 | mediadive.solution:6209 |
| `mediadive_6210_modified_NCL_New_Cereal_Leaf-_Prescott_Liquid.yaml` | CultureMech:014907 | mediadive.solution:6210 |
| `mediadive_6224_0_01_RPA_Rye_Grass_-Prescott_Agar.yaml` | CultureMech:014920 | mediadive.solution:6224 |

For example, CultureMech:014887 is named `3N­BBM+V (Bold Basal Medium with 3­fold Nitrogen  and Vitamins; modified)`. An exact-string search for `3N-BBM+V` does not match it.

## Prose: 57 fields in 47 records

- 34 `preparation_steps[].description` values in 24 records, for example `air­-dried` in `bb_merds.yaml`.
- 23 root `preparation_notes` values in 23 MediaDive solution records.

## Where it comes from

The local raw MediaDive media captures spell `3N-BBM+V` with an ordinary hyphen. They are `data/raw/mediadive/mediadive_media.json` and `data/raw/mediadive_api/mediadive_api_media.json`. I did not find the raw solution payload these six records were built from. So it is unknown whether the MediaDive solution data carries the soft hyphen or an import step introduced it. That should be settled before deciding whether `term.label` should keep the source spelling.

## Suggested fix

1. Move `clean_component_name`, or at least its `_INVISIBLE` table, into a shared helper. Apply it wherever the MediaDive solution importer writes names and labels.
2. Repair the six record names. Append a `curation_history` event, as #409 did with `REMOVED_INVISIBLE_CHARACTERS`.
3. Decide whether to clean the prose fields. They are not identifiers, but they defeat exact-text search.
4. Add a read-only check that fails on these characters in name and label fields, so the next importer cannot reintroduce them.

Related: #387 (closed), #406 (closed), #409.

title: Summary concentration_info lists medium-level and stock-level concentrations without saying which
body:
Found in the second review of #605, at 86d6a1cc.

## Problem

Each occurrence row's `concentration_value` and `concentration_unit` are relative to the row's own container:

- the medium, for a MediaRecipe's root `ingredients`;
- the stock, for a solution record's root `composition`;
- the stock, for an inline stock's `composition` (rows added by #605).

The summaries' `concentration_info` (`mapped_ingredients.yaml`, `unmapped_ingredients.yaml`, built by `_concentration_rows` in `scripts/ingredient_occurrences.py`) is a deduplicated set of `(value, unit, notes)` per ingredient. It has no field that says which container a value belongs to (`MappedConcentrationInfo` in `mapped_ingredients_schema.yaml`). So medium-level and stock-level values sit side by side, indistinguishable.

This predates #605. On `main` at 41d4d390, the TSV rows with a concentration are:

- 165,218 MediaRecipe root rows;
- 34,983 solution-record root rows, already stock-relative.

#605 adds 6,837 inline-stock rows of the same kind. On the full corpus, the second review found 218 mapped identities with numeric values that come only from inline stocks. One example is NaCl (CHEBI:26710), which now also lists `195.0 G_PER_L` from CultureMech:007718 `solutions/0/composition`.

I found no consumer of `concentration_info` in this repo.

## Options

1. Add a scope to each entry, such as the contributing `record_class` and whether the row is root or inline-stock, or simply its `component_field`.
2. Or limit `concentration_info` to medium-level rows, and leave stock-level values to the TSV.

Either choice is a schema and consumer decision, so #605 leaves `concentration_info` as it was and only documents the scope of the TSV columns.

title: Reference validation rejects exact official recipe evidence: brackets, chemical subscripts, and API titles
body:
# Official Recipe Evidence Is Rejected by Reference Validation

Related concentration-repair tracking: #150. This is distinct from #565's
source-check-to-ingredient binding defect.

## Reproduction

Observed on 2026-10-08 in the local concentration-curation worktree at baseline
`f8af2562c3ae51d5f9ed01a484f4a2971b6cd80f`, with
`linkml-reference-validator==0.1.6` and Python 3.13. The new curation records and
reports are not yet committed or published; the underlying public source and
matcher examples below do not require those record edits.

1. **Literal brackets are stripped as though they were citations.** For
   `https://togomedium.org/sparqlist/api/gmdb_medium_by_gmid?gm_id=M1124`, the
   source JSON names `Trace vitamins (see Medium [M190])`. An exact JSON snippet
   including that label and its 10 ml dose is rejected. The error instead
   searches for `Trace vitamins (see Medium  )`.
2. **HTML chemical subscripts change excerpt matching.** At
   `https://www.jcm.riken.jp/cgi-bin/jcm/jcm_grmd?GRMD=1084`, the exact rendered-text
   excerpt `40.0 g FeSO4·7H2O in 0.1 N H2SO4 solution and fill up to 100.0 ml.`
   fails the installed matcher. At JCM1282, `8% (w/v) NaHCO3 solution` also fails.
   Both match whitespace-normalized text extracted from the captured source
   HTML with BeautifulSoup. The chemical numbers must not be discarded.
3. **JSON dataset titles fall back to the URL.** For the TOGO M1153 endpoint,
   the verified `meta.name` is `Thiobacillus Prosperus Medium`. Reference
   validation instead extracts the URL as the title and rejects the correct
   supplied title. The same occurs for M142's `Pyrococcus Medium` and other
   receiving datasets.

The public-source snippet checks can be reproduced using
`SupportingTextValidator(ReferenceValidationConfig(cache_dir=...)).validate(snippet, url)`.
Use a fresh cache to distinguish parser behavior from stale cached content.

## Impact and Evidence

The seven-record nested-stock review adds 206 primary evidence entries.
All 206 snippets are literal matches to hash-pinned HTTP-200 captures; the
installed matcher accepts 200 and rejects six. All seven
`just validate-references <record>` commands fail, also including API title
mismatches. Independent literal checks are not represented as an automated
reference-gate pass.

Local reproducibility artifacts are under
`reports/ingredient_concentration_curation/20261008-m142-nested-traces/`:
`context.json`, `plan.json`, `reference-validation.json`, `audit.py`, and one
report per exact record path. No source quote was rewritten to hide a failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Preserve literal accession brackets in structured-source snippets; do not
  treat `[M190]` as removable Markdown citation syntax.
- Normalize HTML presentation of chemical subscripts consistently without
  losing formula digits, hydrate numbers, signs, units or decimal precision.
- Extract or explicitly support structured recipe titles from the official
  API metadata instead of comparing a verified title with a URL fallback.
- Add fixture-backed positive and negative regressions. Wrong ingredient,
  amount, unit, stock/final scope and title must still fail. Avoid a broad fuzzy
  matcher or disabling title/snippet checks to turn the gate green.
- Re-run the seven records and representative earlier JCM/TOGO cohorts; retain
  distinct reporting for source-access failure, unavailable metadata, a parser
  limitation and a genuine contradiction.

The corpus-wide merge/freshness failures are separate publication blockers.

title: Declare the bundled CommunityMech link return type so the renderer typecheck passes
body:
The required `Changed Python quality + wheel smoke` check fails at the renderer type boundary on PR #559 head `1258379ae693528cc6a0c6f76bbcd9bcf83f162f`.

In `src/culturemech/render_media_pages.py`, `community_links() -> dict[str, str]` returns `json.loads(path.read_text())["links"]` directly. Mypy treats that expression as `Any` and reports:

```text
src/culturemech/render_media_pages.py:96: error: Returning Any from function declared to return "dict[str, str]"  [no-any-return]
```

Reproduction: run `just typecheck-renderer`. The failure is also recorded in [job 112060465655](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CultureMech/actions/runs/37398623932/job/112060465655). Ruff, Black, skill validation and README statistics pass in that job; this is separate from the Black formatting defect in #561.

The local fix makes the bundled JSON return type explicit with `typing.cast(dict[str, str], ...)`, preserving runtime behavior. All nine bundled CommunityMech link entries were checked to have string keys and values, with complete equality before and after the change. No scientific records or link destinations change.

Local verification: renderer mypy passes; all eight changed Python files pass Ruff and Black; 16 renderer/website-audit tests pass; an isolated installed-wheel smoke check passes for the CLI, rendering, EDTA resolution and all nine packaged links. Three fresh render canaries are identical except for their build-signature comment. The untracked local record previews were refreshed by that same signature-only substitution; the Pages workflow renders its own record pages during deployment.

Acceptance:

- [ ] The required renderer typecheck passes without suppressing or disabling `no-any-return`.
- [ ] The packaged CommunityMech link snapshot and rendered record content remain unchanged.
- [ ] Required PR and merge-queue checks pass on the corrected head.

These results describe local verification; the correction has not yet been pushed or deployed.

title: Restore current record navigation and honest lineage in retained media graph views
body:
Both retained media graph views contain broken per-record navigation in the current Pages layout:

- `app/umap.html`: 14,666 derived points and 8,098 direct points.
- `app/umap_graph.html`: the same two populations and counts.

Each click handler assigns `window.location.href = d.url`. All embedded URLs use the old relative `pages/<old-name>.html` shape, so a click from `app/umap.html` resolves under `app/pages/`. That directory is absent, including ignored files. The actual Pages workflow copies `app/` and `pages/` as siblings; normalized current records are generated under `pages/normalized/<CultureMech-local-ID>.html`.

Examples are `pages/2asw.html`, `pages/Artificial_Seawater_Medium.html`, and `pages/DSMZ_1399_HALOPHILIC_MEDIUM.html`. A complete local census found all 22,764 targets missing in each view. The issue predates the pending common-map integration and is separate from the new verified ingredient graph producer. Retaining these useful coordinates should also retain usable navigation and truthful provenance.

Acceptance:
- Resolve historic point identities to current normalized records using explicit, unambiguous source/identifier evidence, not a guessed first label match.
- Preserve existing coordinates and graph population. For unresolved or ambiguous historic points, provide an honest non-broken fallback rather than a fabricated record link.
- Use paths relative to the actual deployed `app/` wrapper, and cover click behavior plus all resolvable point targets with tests.
- Label historical source lineage as unverified unless a real matching provenance receipt exists; do not borrow the new ingredient graph's receipt.

Independent evidence: `workspace/embedding-remediation-20260915/culture-historical-graph-links-review.json` in the coordinating CLAW workspace. All-state searches for graph legacy links, umap links and map 404 found no equivalent issue. Recorded before fixes under CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#426.

title: Bind graph cache reuse to source bytes before issuing provenance
body:
An adversarial review of the embedding rollout reproduced stale graph-vector reuse when compressed source bytes change while basename, byte length and integer mtime remain unchanged. These are currently the graph pickle cache identity fields; they do not establish source-content identity.

The reproduction uses a tiny valid TSV.gz with a header and CHEBI:1. First load: vector [1,0]. Replace the source row with [0,1], preserving byte length and mtime. The next ordinary load returns cached [1,0]. The same behavior was reproduced in CultureMech, MediaIngredientMech and CommunityMech in fresh temporary fixtures; no production source or cache was modified.

This matters for the new provenance work: hashing today's source alongside a stale cache would falsely attribute old vectors to new source bytes. Verified generation must parse and bind the actual selected source, or reuse a cache whose source digest, parser/filter policy and vector bytes are verified together. Existing unverified pickle caches must not be promoted merely by attaching a new receipt.

Acceptance: a regression changing source bytes while preserving size/mtime returns the new vectors (or refuses the old cache); a failed source parse/cache write preserves the previous valid state; freshly generated map receipts bind the actual parsed source and vector bytes. This is a concrete cache-identity subissue of the ongoing graph-provenance rollout coordinated in CultureBotAI/culturebotai-claw#426.

title: has_part edges carry the quantity as one qualifier string; the MediaDive transform kg-microbe ingests carries value and unit columns
body:
Found sizing #374 against the MediaDive transform, and left out of #439 and #443 on purpose.

The MediaDive transform kg-microbe merges today carries a reagent's quantity in two typed edge columns:

```
subject  predicate  object  relation  primary_knowledge_source  knowledge_level  agent_type  value  unit
mediadive.solution:1  biolink:has_part  CHEBI:15377  BFO:0000051  infores:mediadive  observation  manual_agent  1000.0  ml
```

39,755 of its 48,434 `has_part` edges carry a `value`/`unit` pair. Our export packs the same fact into one qualifier string:

```
CultureMech:009646  biolink:has_part  MICRO:0000182  ...  concentration="10.0 G_PER_L"
```

A consumer that sums, converts, or filters by amount can read theirs directly and has to parse ours. When the export replaces the MediaDive transform (#374), every downstream reader of `value`/`unit` on a `has_part` edge loses the column.

Suggested: emit `value` and `unit` as edge columns from `concentration.value` / `concentration.unit` (unit as the enum token, which is already a closed set), keep the `concentration` qualifier for one release so nothing downstream breaks on the same day, and add the two columns to `_QUALIFIER_COLUMNS` and `kgx.yaml` so `tests/test_kgx_tsv_export.py::test_every_qualifier_type_the_transform_emits_has_a_column` covers them. With #443 in, 200,859 `has_part` edges carry a concentration today, so this is the largest single content difference left between the two exports.

title: 4,774 MediaDive solution records carry a 'See source for composition' placeholder ingredient beside a complete composition, and are flagged incomplete

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: Hard stop for agents. Ontology minting, deletions, schema changes.

body:
Found while fixing #442.

Every one of the 4,774 MediaDive solution records carries, beside its real `composition`, an `ingredients` list of exactly one row:

```yaml
ingredients:
- preferred_term: See source for composition
  concentration:
    value: variable
    unit: VARIABLE
data_quality_flags:
- incomplete_composition
```

Measured on `main` at `4c9e47dac5`: 4,774 records, 4,774 placeholder rows, 0 grounded; the same records hold 35,009 grounded `composition` rows. The placeholder is the single string behind the `PLACEHOLDER` class in `just audit-ungrounded-ingredients` (4,775 rows, a third of everything that audit reports, #372 and #407), and the `incomplete_composition` flag on these records is false: their composition is complete, it is in the other list.

Consequences today:

- the ungrounded-ingredient backlog reads 4,775 rows larger than it is, and its ratchet (`--max-names 3217`) carries a name that is not an ingredient;
- `incomplete_composition` cannot be used to find records that are actually incomplete without first excluding these;
- any consumer that reads `ingredients` for a solution record sees "see source" and stops, which is how the exporter emitted nothing for them until #442.

Suggested: drop the placeholder row and the flag from records whose `composition` is non-empty (a bulk mutator; dry-run and a canary first), and have `validate_strict` or a corpus test refuse a placeholder ingredient beside a non-empty composition so the shape cannot return. The `SolutionRecipe` shape should not need an `ingredients` list at all; worth checking whether the importer wrote it to satisfy a MediaRecipe-shaped validator that no longer applies.

title: Solution records mint a node but no composition: transform() never walks top-level composition, 35,009 rows
body:
Found reviewing #439.

#439 gives the 4,784 MediaDive solution records a node each. Their contents still do not reach the graph. `transform()` walks `ingredients[]` and `solutions[].composition[]`, and never a record's top-level `composition[]`, which is where a `SolutionRecipe`-shaped record keeps its reagents:

```
solution records with a top-level composition:   4,784
composition rows in them:                        35,009   (never walked)
solution records that are a has_part subject:    0 of 4,986
```

The other 202 solution records, the curated `record_kind: SOLUTION` ones with `MediaRecipe` shape, do go through `ingredients[]`; they emit nothing because none of the 202 carries a grounded ingredient, which is a curation gap rather than an exporter one.

So a solution node today is a labelled point with no composition, and a medium that references it by name gets no depth through it. For #374 this is the content that matters most: the MediaDive transform's 45,225 `solution → ingredient` edges are the bulk of its composition depth, and the corresponding rows are sitting in these records.

Two smaller things in the same area, both visible in #439's diff:

- 202 solution records carry a `medium_type`. `nodes()` types them `biolink:ChemicalMixture` (correct) and then still mints a `medium_type_*` node and a `has_attribute` edge for them, which is a medium's attribute on a mixture. Addressed in #439.
- `is_solution_record` in the exporter duplicates `scripts/record_kinds.py` (0 disagreements across 15,877 records today). A shared module under `src/` would stop them drifting.

Suggested: walk top-level `composition[]` for solution records with the existing `ingredient_to_edge`, carrying `value`/`unit` as #374 wants, and gate the export on the count of solution records that emit at least one `has_part` so the 0 above cannot come back.

title: CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT names the wrapper directory while COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT names the repository
body:
Found reviewing #431.

`CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT` names the *wrapper* directory, and the code appends the 
repository name to it:

```python
CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT = Path(os.environ.get("CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT", REPO_ROOT.parent / "CultureBotHT"))
...
default=CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT / "CultureBotHT",
```

The doubling is faithful to the real layout, which genuinely nests 
(`.../KG-Hub/KG-Microbe/CultureBotHT/CultureBotHT`), so this is a contract 
problem rather than a wrong path. The obvious reading of a variable called 
`<PROJECT>_ROOT` is "the root of that project". Anyone who sets it to the 
repository, which is the thing they actually have a path to, gets 
`<repo>/CultureBotHT` and a not-found error naming a directory one level below 
what they typed. The docstring explains the nesting, but the failure surfaces at 
the shell, not in the source.

The sibling default is separately dead under the current layout: the Mech 
checkouts moved to `.../ontology/Mechs/` on 2026-09-07, `CultureBotHT` is not 
among them, and it still sits under the old `KG-Hub/KG-Microbe/` tree. So the 
default resolves to nothing on this machine and the variable is the only working 
route, which makes its contract the whole interface.

Compare `COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT` in the same PR, which names the repository directly 
and appends only `data/embeddings`. The two new variables read the same and mean 
different things.

Nothing depends on the current spelling yet, since both variables ship in #431, 
so the contract is free to fix now and expensive later.

Suggested: let `CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT` name the repository, matching 
`COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT`, and keep the nesting only in the sibling fallback.

title: An exported-but-empty COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT or CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT silently becomes the working directory
body:
Found reviewing #431.

Both new environment overrides use `os.environ.get(NAME, default)`. That default 
applies only when the variable is *absent*. Exported-and-empty is a distinct and 
common shell state, and it yields `Path("")`, which is `Path(".")`:

```
>>> os.environ['X'] = ''
>>> Path(os.environ.get('X', 'fallback'))
PosixPath('.')
>>> Path(os.environ.get('X', 'fallback')) / 'data' / 'embeddings'
PosixPath('data/embeddings')
```

So `COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT=` turns the embeddings fallback into a cwd-relative 
`data/embeddings/...`, and `CULTUREBOTHT_ROOT=` turns the importer default into 
`CultureBotHT/` under the cwd. Both then fail as "not found" pointing at a path 
the user never named, which is the confusing failure the sibling fallback exists 
to avoid. An empty export happens easily, e.g. `export COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT=$UNSET_VAR`.

Affected:
- `scripts/generate_ingredient_umap.py:38`
- `scripts/import_from_culturebotht.py:36`

Suggested: treat empty as absent, `os.environ.get(NAME) or default`.

title: generate_ingredient_umap derives a sibling checkout from an unresolved __file__
body:
Found reviewing #431.

`scripts/generate_ingredient_umap.py:29` keeps `_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent`, 
unresolved. The other two scripts the PR touched both use `.resolve()`:

| script | root |
|---|---|
| `export_mediadive_composition.py:20` | `Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent` |
| `import_from_culturebotht.py:33` | `Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent` |
| `generate_ingredient_umap.py:29` | `Path(__file__).parent.parent` |

Before #431 this did not matter: `_REPO_ROOT` was only joined downward, into the 
checkout, where an unresolved prefix is harmless. The PR makes it load-bearing 
*upward* by deriving a sibling from it:

```python
_COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT = Path(os.environ.get("COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT", _REPO_ROOT.parent / "CommunityMech"))
```

`_REPO_ROOT.parent` is the parent of wherever the symlink lives, not the parent of 
the real checkout, so under a symlinked checkout the sibling lookup searches the 
wrong directory and the embeddings fallback silently misses. Line 48 derives the 
claw workspace the same way and inherits it.

Suggested: add `.resolve()`, matching the two siblings.

title: The machine-independent-path guard scans scripts/ only, so two live hardcodes under src/ stay invisible
body:
Found reviewing #431.

`tests/test_scripts_are_machine_independent.py` globs `scripts/*.py`. That is 
non-recursive and excludes `src/`, so the guard covers a directory rather than the 
bug class it is named for. Two files under `src/` carry the identical hardcode the 
PR set out to remove:

| file | line | value |
|---|---|---|
| `src/culturemech/import/import_cofactors.py` | 10 | `PFAS_REPO = Path("/Users/marcin/Documents/VIMSS/ontology/PFAS/PFASCommunityAgents")` |
| `src/culturemech/import/import_ingredient_roles.py` | 13 | same literal |

Both are reachable, not dead code: `just import-pfas-roles` and 
`just import-pfas-cofactors` invoke them as `python -m culturemech.import.*` 
(`project.justfile:2537`, `project.justfile:2546`).

The PR's own predicate returns `True` for both, so this is scope, not detection:

```
src/culturemech/import/import_cofactors.py       -> True
src/culturemech/import/import_ingredient_roles.py -> True
```

Unlike the three scripts #431 fixes, that path still exists on this machine, so 
these two are not broken today. They are the same one-laptop dependency, and the 
new guard is shaped so it can never report them.

Scanning `src/` too means the `Documents/` branch of the regex will also reach 
prose files if the glob is widened further; keep the guard on Python sources 
(`scripts/*.py` plus `src/**/*.py`) rather than all tracked text.

Suggested: widen the glob to both trees, and derive `PFAS_REPO` from 
`PFASCOMMUNITYAGENTS_ROOT` with a sibling-checkout fallback, the pattern #431 
already uses.

title: Two scripts hardcode an absolute checkout path that no longer exists
body:
Two tracked scripts embed one developer's absolute checkout path, so they run on one machine only. Since 2026-09-07 that path no longer exists even there (the Mech checkouts moved to `ontology/Mechs/`).

| script | line | literal | what it should be |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `scripts/export_mediadive_composition.py` | 19 | `OUTPUT_DIR = Path("/Users/marcin/Documents/VIMSS/ontology/KG-Hub/KG-Microbe/CultureMech/data/raw/mediadive")` | `REPO_ROOT / "data/raw/mediadive"`, the idiom 50 other scripts here use |
| `scripts/generate_ingredient_umap.py` | 34 | `"/Users/marcin/Documents/VIMSS/ontology/KG-Hub/KG-Microbe/CommunityMech/CommunityMech/data/embeddings/..."` as the sibling-repo fallback for the embeddings file | `COMMUNITYMECH_ROOT` from the environment, falling back to `_REPO_ROOT.parent / "CommunityMech"`, which is the fleet's convention |

The first writes MediaDive export output; on any other machine it fails to create the directory. The second is a fallback that only fires when `data/embeddings/` is absent, so it fails silently in the sense that the error names a path nobody else has.

Found by claw's fleet-wide search while fixing the same class in claw (culturebotai-claw#365). No test here guards against absolute paths in `scripts/`; `tests/test_domain_growth_evidence.py` mentions `/Users/` for a different reason. Worth adding the guard alongside the fix so the class does not come back.

title: The schema-gap-analysis snapshot describes a corpus that no longer exists
body:
Found while canonicalising this skill from claw (culturebotai-claw#342).

`.claude/skills/schema-gap-analysis/SKILL.md` carries a table headed **"CultureMech-specific
gap classes (current state, 2026-05-17 pass)"**:

| Count | Error | claimed |
|---:|---|---|
| 1,195 | `Additional properties are not allowed ('date')` + `'timestamp' is a required property` | top finding |
| … | | |
| **2,943** | total errors across **4,289** records | |

Measured against `origin/main` on 2026-09-04:

```
$ git ls-files 'data/merge_yaml/merged/*.yaml' | wc -l
6286
$ git grep -c "^  date:" -- data/merge_yaml/merged | wc -l
0
$ git grep -l "timestamp:" -- data/merge_yaml/merged | wc -l
6286
```

The corpus is **46% larger** than the table says, and the headline defect is **entirely
fixed** — zero records carry the old `date` key and all 6,286 carry `timestamp`. Every number
in the table is wrong.

Nothing flagged it, because prose has no test. The table has read as current fact for three
and a half months, and anyone onboarding through this skill starts by looking for 1,195
failures that are not there.

## The fix already exists in the fleet

TraitMech's `audit-schema-gaps` lists exactly this as an anti-pattern — *"Do not present a
snapshot count as current repository state"* — and its `schema-gap-analysis` alias deletes
its own snapshot in favour of the commands that regenerate one:

> Read live command output and the artifacts those commands regenerate. Do not infer corpus
> size, writer coverage, or validation status from prose.

Suggested: replace the table's *counts* with the command that produces them, and keep the
**classes** — what each error looks like, which axis it belongs to, why it recurs. Those are
stable and genuinely useful; the tallies have a short half-life.

CommunityMech carries a dated snapshot of the same shape and is filed separately.

The claw template for this skill now makes "do not write down the state" a managed region,
with this measurement as its evidence.

title: Nothing tests that a MIM pin bump preserves resolution answers; the pin test only checks row count, commit, and hash
body:
Found reviewing #415.

## What exists today

`tests/test_mim_label_index.py::test_packaged_artifact_is_verified_and_pinned`
asserts three scalars:

```python
assert len(index.rows) == 9876
assert index.metadata["source_commit"] == "9f09e4fb..."
assert index.metadata["sha256"] == "a36cd468..."
```

Those catch a *corrupt or unintended* artifact. They say nothing about whether
the new artifact still answers the same questions. A handful of individual
resolutions are pinned nearby (EDTA → `CHEBI:4735`, Beef heart →
`FOODON:00004410`, PABA → `CHEBI:30753`, 1,3-Hexanediol → `cas:21531-91-9`), and
`just check-mim-label-index` validates the artifact's internal consistency, but
neither compares old behaviour to new.

So the safety question a bump actually raises — *does any label that resolved
before now resolve differently, or not at all?* — is answered only by reading
the refresh script's stdout by hand at bump time, and that output is not
recorded anywhere.

## Why it matters

For #415 I answered it manually by replaying every label through the real
resolver under both pins:

```
labels tested : 9115
same answer   : 9092
LOST          : 0
gained        : 8
moved         : 15     (all kgmicrobe.compound:* -> real ChEBI terms)
```

That is exactly the evidence a reviewer needs, and it took a throwaway script.
The next bump gets it only if whoever does it thinks to write the same script
again. A bump that silently dropped 50 resolutions would pass every check in the
repo, because the row count would still match the new metadata and the hash
would still match the new file.

The same replay also surfaced two things worth asserting permanently:

- **No unknown enum values.** `SAFE_AMBIGUITIES`, `MATCH_TYPES` and
  `MAPPING_STATUSES` are closed sets in `mim_label_index.py`. MIM grows these
  organically. A new `ambiguity` value would arrive with no test to catch it.
  (Checked for #415: none.)
- **No safe→unsafe ambiguity transitions.** Those fail closed, so a label can
  stop resolving while remaining present in the file — invisible to a row-count
  or set-difference check. (Checked for #415: zero.)

## Suggested shape

A helper that, given two `label_index.csv` revisions, replays every label of the
older one through `MIMLabelIndex.resolve_label` and reports
`same / lost / gained / moved` with examples — invoked by the refresh script and
printed alongside the existing `+N -M changed=K` line, so the delta lands in the
PR description by construction. Plus unit assertions that every enum column
value in the packaged artifact is a member of its closed set.

Not addressed in #415, which is a data-only bump; this is test infrastructure and
would want its own review.

title: TOGO import substitutes G_PER_L for volume units: 3,803 rows, of which 1,224 are non-water and numerically wrong
body:
Found while verifying the source spelling for #406 — the raw TOGO capture is
tracked, so the import can be compared against it directly.

## The substitution

`data/raw/togo/togo_media.json` records each component's own unit. Comparing
2,900 matched TOGO media, component by component:

```
comparable rows                                32,841
source unit is a VOLUME (ml, ml/l, L, ul)       3,808
  -> recorded as G_PER_L                        3,803
  -> recorded as ML_PER_L or L                      2
```

The unit is not converted, it is **replaced**. `CultureMech:008849`
(`TOGO:M2262`, PCR-S11 medium) side by side with its source:

| ingredient | TOGO says | record says |
|---|---|---|
| Seawater (autoclaved) | 1000 **ml** | 1000 **G_PER_L** |
| Trace metals 'Gaffron+Se' | 0.5 **ml/l** | 0.5 **G_PER_L** |
| 50mM NaH2PO4 | 100 **ml** | 100 **G_PER_L** |
| 0.1N HCl | 40 **ml** | 40 **G_PER_L** |
| (NH4)2SO4 | 400 uM | 400 MICROMOLAR ✅ |
| Vitamin B12 | 10 ug/L | 10 MICROG_PER_L ✅ |
| Hepes | 119.15 g | 119.15 G_PER_L ✅ |

Molar and mass units convert correctly. Only volumes are mislabelled, and the
schema already has `ML_PER_L` and `L` for them.

## Where it is and is not defensible

**Water — 2,579 rows.** Water's density is 1, so `1000 ml -> 1000 g/L` is
numerically near-exact. Ugly, and it is what feeds `WATER_AS_VOLUME` in
`audit-concentration-plausibility`, but not a wrong quantity.

**Everything else — 1,224 rows across 751 records.** The density is not 1, so
the number itself is wrong:

| ingredient | rows | density | error |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| `HCl (25%; 7.7 M)` | 72 | ~1.12 | 12% low |
| `Methanol` | 26 | 0.792 | 26% high |
| `Glycerol` | 21 | 1.26 | 21% low |
| `Tween 80` | 20 | 1.06 | |
| `Ethanol` | 14 | 0.789 | 27% high |
| `Sol. 1`, `Artificial seawater`, `Seawater`, `NaOH 1 N`, ... | | | |

`0.5 ml/l` of a trace-metal stock recorded as `0.5 g/L` is not a rounding
difference — it is a different physical quantity, and nothing downstream can
tell.

## No gate sees the non-water half

`audit-concentration-plausibility` has `WATER_AS_VOLUME` (water >= 1000 G_PER_L),
which is why the water rows are already inside #150's backlog. Methanol at
`792 G_PER_L`, glycerol at `50 G_PER_L` and HCl at `40 G_PER_L` match no
detector — not a trace salt, not an indicator, not water.

## Suggested

1. Map source volume units onto `ML_PER_L` / `L` at import rather than
   defaulting to `G_PER_L`. The enum values exist.
2. Repair the 1,224 non-water rows from the tracked raw capture, which holds
   the original unit — so this is a relabelling, not a re-derivation, and needs
   no source lookup.
3. Decide the water case deliberately: `2,579` rows are numerically fine and
   semantically wrong, and they currently inflate `WATER_AS_VOLUME`.
4. Check whether the same substitution exists in the other volume-bearing
   importers (MediaDive, KOMODO, JCM) — this was found by comparing against a
   tracked raw capture, which not every source has.

Related: #150 (the plausibility backlog the water half sits in), #381 (absolute
amounts with no representable unit), #394 (a different import-time arithmetic
defect), #406 (the record this was found from).

title: cleanup_media_quality summed duplicate ingredient rows: 292 agar rows are physically impossible and no gate sees them
body:
Found while triaging #283, which turns out to be one instance of a much larger
pattern.

## The mutator

`scripts/cleanup_media_quality.py:149` merges duplicate ingredient rows by
**adding their concentrations**:

```python
total = sum(concentrations)
...
base['notes'] += f' [Merged {len(group)} duplicates: {", ".join(map(str, concentrations))}]'
```

It records exactly what it did, which is how this was findable:

```yaml
- preferred_term: Agar
  concentration: {value: '50.0', unit: G_PER_L}
  notes: ' (for solid medium) [Merged 3 duplicates: 15.0, 15.0, 20.0]'
```

15 + 15 + 20 = 50.

## Why summing is the wrong operation here

Duplicate rows for one ingredient usually mean the *same* addition was listed
twice by the importer, not that the medium receives the ingredient twice.
Summing turns a transcription artifact into a fabricated quantity.

For agar it is unambiguous. Agar is a solidifier that sets at **15-20 g/L**;
above roughly 30 g/L the medium will not pour and the value cannot be real.

```
Agar, G_PER_L, corpus-wide:
   2132 rows @ 15.0     <- normal
    574 rows @ 20       <- normal
    186 rows @ 50.0     <- 15+15+20
     65 rows @ 65.0
  ...
  rows above 30 g/L: 292
```

## Scale

| | count |
|---|--:|
| ingredient rows carrying a `[Merged N duplicates: ...]` note | **5,081** |
| ...across records | **2,667** |
| ...whose value equals the **sum** of the listed parts | **4,503** |
| agar rows above 30 g/L | **292** |
| records where a merged row **coexists** with another row of the same name | **276** |

Most affected ingredients: NaCl (981), Distilled water (840), CaCl2 x 2 H2O
(662), MgSO4 x 7 H2O (417), Agar (267).

That last row of the table is a second defect on top of the first: the merge
left a row behind, so `KOMODO_457_MINERAL_MEDIUM_BRUNNER.yaml` carries **both**
`Agar 50.0` and `Agar 15.0`. Whatever consumes it double-counts.

## Not all of it is wrong, which is the difficulty

`JCM_J151_PYROCOCCUS_MEDIUM` has `NaCl 14.85 = 13.85 + 1.0`, which may be a
legitimate total of two additions. `MnCl2 x 4 H2O 0.1018 = 0.0018 + 0.1` is a
trace element summed with what looks like a stock-strength value, and is not.
So this is not a blanket revert — the provable subset is where the summed value
is physically impossible for the substance.

## No gate sees it

`audit-concentration-plausibility` has three detectors — `WATER_AS_VOLUME`,
`TRACE_SALT_AS_STOCK`, `INDICATOR_UNIT_SLIP`. Agar is neither a trace salt nor
an indicator, and 50 g/L is below the water threshold. Confirmed: **zero rows
whose ingredient is agar appear in `concentration_plausibility.tsv`.**

The other two PR-blocking gates (`validate-strict`, `check-chebi-grounding`)
check shape and grounding, not plausibility of a value against its substance.

## Proposed work

1. A detector for duplicate ingredient rows within one record, classifying
   exact duplicates, power-of-ten pairs (#283), and merged-sum survivors.
2. A solidifier plausibility detector, so an impossible agar value fails rather
   than passing three green gates.
3. Repair only the provable subset. The agar case has a defensible target — the
   note preserves the original parts, so the pre-merge value is recoverable
   from the record itself without inventing anything.
4. Fix `cleanup_media_quality.py` so it cannot do this again.

Relates to #283 (one record of pattern 1), #150 (the plausibility backlog this
should not silently inflate), and #302 (why a total-based ratchet would hide a
repair here).

title: 618 ingredient mentions carry parse damage as their preferred_term; all 497 numeric ones are recoverable
body:
Found while triaging the ingredient labels MIM cannot resolve
(MediaIngredientMech `scripts/triage_culturemech_residual.py`). 24 distinct
`preferred_term` values covering **618 recipe mentions** are not ingredient names at all.
The damage is in `data/normalized_yaml/` itself, not introduced by the occurrence
exporter, so it dates from recipe ingestion.

Two distinct defects.

## 1. Field swap: the quantity is in `preferred_term`, the name is in `notes` (497 mentions)

```
CultureMech:000001  preferred_term: "1"  notes: "Original amount: DYIII Medium"
CultureMech:000001  preferred_term: "2"  notes: "Original amount: Pea"
CultureMech:000002  preferred_term: "1"  notes: "Original amount: CR1 Soil"
CultureMech:000002  preferred_term: "2"  notes: "Original amount: MgCO3(MCIB CB486)"
```

`preferred_term` holds the ingredient's list index while the actual name sits in `notes`.
**All 497 of these carry an `Original amount:` note, so the name is recoverable for 100% of
them** -- this is a remapping, not a re-scrape. Affected values are the bare numbers 1-13.

## 2. A Python list repr split on commas (121 mentions)

| mentions | preferred_term |
|---:|---|
| 75 | `'Iron(III` |
| 13 | `'Fe(III` |
| 8 | `'Chromium(III` |
| 6 | `'(S` |
| 2 | `'Manganese(IV` |
| 2 | `'(9Z` |
| 1 | `'Nickel(II` |
| 1 | `'Cyanocob(III` |

Note the leading apostrophe on each. From `data/normalized_yaml/`, verbatim:

    - preferred_term: '''Iron(III'
      concentration:
        value: '0.04994'

That apostrophe is a Python string quote, and every value truncates at the first comma
inside a chemical name -- `Iron(III), citrate` and `(9Z,12Z)-octadecadienoate` split at
their internal comma. A `str()` of a list was written where the list elements were meant,
then re-split on `", "`. The oxidation-state Roman numerals and stereodescriptors are
exactly the names that contain commas, which is why they are the ones that broke.

Unlike defect 1 these are lossy -- the tail of each name became a separate fragment or was
dropped -- so they need re-derivation from the source recipe rather than a field move.

## Why it matters

These 618 mentions are permanently unresolvable against MIM: no ontology will ever contain
a term called `1` or `'Iron(III`, so they sit in MIM's residual forever and inflate the
apparent size of the ingredient-grounding backlog. MIM's triage now classifies them as
`NOISE` and routes them out of the grounding work, but the fix belongs here.

Evidence table: MIM `reports/culturemech_residual_triage.tsv`, rows whose `bucket` starts
with `NOISE`.

title: Absolute ingredient amounts survive only as prose: 120 UTEX rows are VARIABLE because the unit enum has no bare mL or g
body:
Found reviewing #378.

`ConcentrationUnitEnum` is entirely ratios plus two escapes:

```
G_PER_L, MG_PER_L, MICROG_PER_L, MOLAR, MILLIMOLAR, MICROMOLAR,
PERCENT_W_V, PERCENT_V_V, ML_PER_L, MG_PER_ML, FOLD_DILUTION, L, VARIABLE
```

There is no bare `ML`, `G`, or `MG`. So an amount stated without a volume basis
cannot be represented, and #378 records it as
`{value: variable, unit: VARIABLE}` with the source text in `notes`:

```yaml
- preferred_term: DYIII Medium
  concentration: {value: variable, unit: VARIABLE}
  notes: 'UTEX lists: amount 90 mL'
```

That is honest — it is a large improvement on the fabricated `G_PER_L` it
replaced — but the number is now only machine-readable by parsing prose. **120
of 497 repaired UTEX ingredients** are in this state. Affected shapes, all real:
`90 mL`, `4 drops`, `1 cc`, `1 tsp`, `1 per 200 mL`, `40 mL of supernatant`.

Note `L` already exists as an *absolute* volume unit, so the enum is not
consistently ratio-only — `ML` is missing rather than deliberately excluded.

## The modelling question

A 1:1 mixture medium genuinely has no per-litre concentration; `90 mL of DYIII
+ 90 mL of Soilwater` is a ratio between components, not a concentration in a
solvent. Options, roughly in order of increasing scope:

1. Add `ML`, `G`, `MG` for absolute amounts, leaving the basis to
   `ConcentrationValue.per_volume`.
2. Use `per_volume` alone with an existing unit, which is contradictory today
   (`MG_PER_L` + `per_volume: "per 12 mL"` states two different bases).
3. A separate `amount` field distinct from `concentration`, which is what UTEX
   and several other sources actually publish.

Non-metric amounts (`drops`, `tsp`, `cc`) are a separate problem and probably
stay `VARIABLE` regardless — `cc` is unambiguously mL, but `drops` is not a
unit.

Worth deciding deliberately rather than by default, since it affects every
source that publishes per-batch amounts, not just UTEX.

title: Define a fleet behavioral contract for provider triage
body:
## Adversarial review finding

The provider-triage implementation is now committed on `main` in all five Mech repositories, but there is no fleet-level behavioral contract protecting the parts that should agree.

Current GitHub blob identities are all different:

| repository | `scripts/deep_research_provider.py` blob |
|---|---|
| CultureMech | `790223960de2c9758e57903e08bdc5b3c2303852` |
| TraitMech | `9f57334b525e680f2acfca644c31008cafdd7b72` |
| MediaIngredientMech | `d00d1851eed987575ce2d4895f8605642712431b` |
| CommunityMech | `2dcdf2595ee1aa3b89d408d325991b205e3e594d` |
| proteintraitsmech | `3bd6e03a76a394d5b1285297b9b5760fbb987133` |

Some divergence is correct: each Mech has custom research focuses, and TraitMech exposes a richer `configured` / `available` / `routable` availability model with injected environment state. Other behavior should remain aligned: absolute fit semantics, negative-score ordering, provider filters, allowlists, no-paid policy, selected-provider JSON consistency, deterministic ties, and credit-free inspection.

The existing byte-exact vendored-sync mechanism is therefore the wrong gate for this script. It would either reject valid domain specialization or leave common routing semantics ungoverned.

This supersedes the future-looking portion of #287. That issue was correctly closed when these files existed only as untracked local copies; they are now public and the premise has materially changed.

## Proposed scope

1. Define a small provider-triage contract fixture covering shared inputs and observable outputs.
2. Run the same fixture against every Mech implementation without invoking a provider.
3. Keep focus definitions, domain weights, provider descriptions, and target resolution local.
4. Document intentional extensions, including TraitMech's richer availability state, without requiring the other Mechs to erase them.
5. Add a fleet check or reusable test package so a routing-policy change cannot silently drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- All five implementations pass the same contract for fit normalization and deterministic ordering, including all-negative raw scores.
- Provider-filtered output cannot select or recommend a provider omitted from its ranking.
- Allowlists and no-paid-provider policy have the same externally visible semantics.
- Inspection and contract tests perform no provider call and spend no provider credits.
- Domain-specific focuses and weights remain local and schema-validated.
- Intentional implementation differences are listed in one maintained compatibility document.

Found during the five-Mech alignment and adversarial provider-assignment review.
